Use the Pylon CLI to access the Pylon API from your terminal or scripts.

The CLI is experimental. The current release is v0.1.1 and may change. The SDKs are versioned separately; upgrading an SDK does not upgrade the CLI.

## Install

With Homebrew on macOS or Linux:

```
brew install pylon-labs/tap/pylon
pylon --version
```

For Windows or installation without Homebrew, download an installer or binary for your platform from GitHub Releases.

## Authenticate

Create a Pylon API token as described in Authentication, then run:

```
pylon auth login --with-token
```

Paste your token into the hidden prompt. The CLI saves it for future requests. On macOS, it uses Keychain when available. For automation, you can provide the token through the `PYLON_TOKEN` environment variable instead.

Confirm your connection:

```
pylon me get
```

Requests use the permissions associated with your API token.

### EU organizations

The CLI uses the US API by default. For an EU organization, add `--base-url` to your requests:

You can also set `PYLON_BASE_URL=https://api.eu.usepylon.com` in your environment.

## Try a few read commands

List five accounts:

Get an issue by its ID or number, replacing `1234` with your issue number:

Explore commands and their parameters:

JSON is the default in terminals and pipes. It includes the full API response, including nested fields and pagination metadata. Use `--format table` for a human-readable table or `--query` to select fields:

List commands fetch one page by default. Add `--page-all` to fetch every page. For example, export account responses as one JSON page per line:

Use `--page-limit N` to set a page cap. The CLI warns if more results remain. Failed requests return a nonzero exit code, even if earlier pages have already been printed.

Pylon’s API can be used to programmatically access and take action on data within Pylon.

Only Admin users can create API tokens. To learn more about Admins, see Roles & User Management.

Some common use cases for our API include:

* Fetching information about customers
* Fetching information about issues
* Creating issues programmatically

Check out our API Reference for specifications on all endpoints. To call the API from TypeScript, Python, or Go, use our SDKs.

Before you build an integration, read:

* Authentication for creating tokens, roles, and regions
* API conventions for IDs, timestamps, pagination, search filters, update behavior, files, and slugs
* Rate limits for request limits and how to handle `429` responses
* Errors for error codes and response format

# Pylon MCP server

Connect ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor to Pylon. Work issues, accounts, contacts, and your knowledge base with the permissions you already have.

Thank you! Your submission has been received!

Oops! Something went wrong while submitting the form.

Trusted by 1,800+ B2B customers globally

What is Pylon’s MCP server?

Deploy AI agents that handle questions end-to-end, gather context for your team, and escalate to humans when it matters.

Can ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor use Pylon data?

Yes. Point a supported MCP client at your regional Pylon MCP URL, sign in with OAuth or use an API token, and work issues, accounts, contacts, and your knowledge base from the AI tool you already use. For ChatGPT, you can also install Pylon’s native ChatGPT app from Settings > Plugins (some older views, including very old iOS or Android apps, show Apps instead of Plugins). See how to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP.

Is access scoped to each user?

Yes. Every action runs as the authenticated user. The server cannot return data that user cannot see in Pylon, or write changes that user cannot already make in the UI. Connecting needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include.

Can engineers investigate from their editor?

Yes. Tools like Claude Code or Cursor can open a Pylon issue, pull message history, and keep working in the same flow your team already uses for debugging. Opening a pull request still depends on that coding tool’s own GitHub or codebase connection, not on a Pylon MCP "create PR" tool.

Can you turn support evidence into docs and analysis?

Yes. Feed issue context into an AI tool to draft an internal note, a product brief, or an account summary, and combine Pylon data with other sources those tools can reach (for example Notion or Linear) when those connections are configured.

How do you set up the Pylon MCP server?

Step 1

Enable MCP Access

Make sure each user or API token identity that connects has the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Access follows the same scoping as the Pylon dashboard.

Step 2

Open the MCP Server settings in Pylon

In Pylon, go to Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server. Copy your workspace’s regional MCP URL from Installation.

Step 3

Connect your AI tool

Add the URL in your AI tool’s MCP settings, or for ChatGPT install the Pylon app from Settings > Plugins. Auth is OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Transport is Streamable HTTP (stateless).

US server: mcp.usepylon.com

EU server: mcp.eu.usepylon.com

See Pylon’s MCP docs for the full tool list.

See the MCP setup guide for client steps.

See how to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP.

See how to connect Pylon to Claude with MCP.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Pylon MCP server?

MCP is an open standard that lets AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor connect to external products. Pylon’s MCP server exposes your Pylon workspace (issues, accounts, contacts, and more) to those tools over OAuth 2.0 or an API token, so your team can query and act on support data from the AI clients they already use.

Which AI tools can connect to Pylon via MCP?

Pylon’s MCP server works with MCP clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, and Cursor. For ChatGPT, the fastest path is Pylon’s native ChatGPT app; you can also add the regional MCP URL as a custom connector. Headless workers, scripts, and clients that support custom authorization headers can connect with an existing Pylon API token instead of OAuth.

What actions can an AI tool take in Pylon through MCP?

Connected AI tools can search and update issues, post internal notes, and send customer replies, which AI tools are instructed to show you for approval before sending. They can also manage accounts and contacts, draft and publish knowledge base articles, and work with macros, tags, and triggers. Tools for tasks, projects, account notes, and call recordings require Account Intelligence. Feature requests and some other tools require additional plan features. All actions stay within your Pylon permissions.

Is the Pylon MCP server secure?

Connections use OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Actions run as the signed-in user or the token’s identity, with that identity’s current role and permissions. No extra permissions are granted. The identity also needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include.

How do I set up the Pylon MCP server?

Open Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server in Pylon, copy your regional URL (https://mcp.usepylon.com or https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com), and add it in your AI tool (or install the ChatGPT app). Sign in with OAuth, or send an existing API token in an Authorization: Bearer header if your client supports it.

Is the Pylon MCP server on every plan?

Yes. The pricing Features by tier table lists the Pylon MCP server on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise. Some individual MCP tools still require add-ons or plan features such as Account Intelligence.

# How do I connect to the Pylon MCP Server?

Last updated 25 days ago

The Pylon MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com provides AI tools access to your Pylon data. The endpoint uses HTTPS, so the connection is protected with TLS. It uses OAuth authentication with your Pylon account.

The application you connect to Pylon's MCP will only have access to data you would have access to in Pylon, and will read and write on behalf of you.

## Common Clients

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add pylon --transport http https://mcp.usepylon.com/
```

Then, in Claude Code, run the `/mcp` command and select the `pylon` MCP to authenticate.

`--transport http` selects MCP's Streamable HTTP transport and stateless request handling; it does not mean that the connection is unencrypted or uses a plaintext HTTP URL. The Pylon endpoint remains HTTPS/TLS-protected.

### Claude Desktop and Web

In "Admin Settings", add a custom connector named "Pylon" with URL `https://mcp.usepylon.com/`

Leave "OAuth Client ID" and "OAuth Client Secret" blank.

Navigate to "Settings > Connectors" and click the "Connect" button next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

### ChatGPT

In the Apps tab, search for Pylon and install our native ChatGPT app.

### Cursor

Add to your Cursor MCP settings:

`~/.cursor/mcp.json` :

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    ...
    "pylon": {
      "url": "https://mcp.usepylon.com/"
    }
    ...
  }
}
```

Navigate to "Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP" and click "Connect" next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

## Authentication Flow

**Note:** The Pylon MCP server only supports OAuth authentication. API key authentication is not currently available, which may affect usage in remote environments or platforms that don't support OAuth for remote connections.

**Current capabilities:** The Pylon MCP server provides access to issues, accounts, and contacts, as well as knowledge base articles and collections, macros, tags, and triggers. Tools for tasks, projects, and account notes require Account Intelligence. Available tools can also vary by organization and tool-specific feature flag. Registering a tool does not mean it will appear or be usable in every organization. All tool calls are also subject to the authenticated user's applicable Pylon permissions.

The MCP server does not currently support fetching notebook block content directly. To use notebook content in external tools like Claude, manually open the Account Overview notebook, copy the rendered text block output, and paste it into your conversation as context.

1. When the MCP client connects, it will open your browser

2. Log in with your Pylon account credentials

3. Authorize the MCP connection

4. The browser will redirect back and complete the OAuth flow

5. Your MCP client is now connected to Pylon!

**Headless or bot-only clients:** The Pylon MCP server does not currently support API keys, machine-to-machine credentials, or other non-OAuth authentication methods. If your client cannot complete the browser-based OAuth flow, it cannot connect directly to the Pylon MCP server today.

If you need token-based access for a supported integration or automation, use the Pylon REST API instead of MCP. The REST API accepts Bearer API tokens, but that authentication method does not apply to the Pylon MCP server.

## Session Expiry and Reconnecting

OAuth sessions expire periodically. The exact duration varies by MCP client - some sessions last a few hours, others can last several days.

When your session expires, you may see authentication errors or your MCP tools may stop returning results. To reconnect, simply re-authenticate through the same flow you used during initial setup:

* **Claude Code:** Run `/mcp` and re-authenticate the Pylon connection
* **Claude Desktop/Web:** Go to **Settings > Connectors** and click "Connect" next to Pylon
* **Cursor:** Go to **Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP** and click "Connect" next to Pylon

This is normal behavior and not a bug. If you find yourself needing to reconnect unusually frequently (e.g. multiple times per day), please reach out to support.

## Use case examples

* **Debug an issue end to end:** Solve an issue with Claude Code with a prompt like "debug this <pylon link>" and put up a PR for a bug fix
* **Write a product spec notion doc:** Feed it a bunch of issues and use a Claude Code skill to generate a product spec doc based on evidence
* **Ad hoc analysis:** Ask a question about a customer in ChatGPT and leverage data from Pylon in addition to other tools like Notion or Linear

**Seat requirement:** You need a **Member** or **Admin** seat to connect to the MCP server. Viewer and Integration users cannot authenticate and will see an "Authorization failed" error. If you hit this, ask your workspace admin to upgrade your seat type in **Settings > Users**.

# Authentication
How to authenticate with Pylon's API
The Pylon API uses [Bearer](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750#section-2.1) authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:
```
Authorization: Bearer 
```
{% hint style="info" %}
Generate an API token in the [Pylon dashboard](https://app.usepylon.com/settings/api-tokens).
{% endhint %}
### API regions
Pylon’s API is available in two regions. Use the base URL that matches where your Pylon tenant is hosted:
\* US region: 
\* EU region: 
Both regions use the same API endpoints and authentication. Configure your integration to use the region where your Pylon tenant is hosted.
You can tell a token's region from its prefix:
| Prefix | Region |
| --------------- | ------ |
| `pylon\_api\_eu\_` | EU |
| `pylon\_api\_` | US |
Tokens created before prefixes were introduced have no prefix. Sending a token to the other region's API returns `401` with the `wrong\_region\_token` error code, and the message names the correct URL.
Once you've created a token, call the [`/me`](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference/me.md) endpoint to retrieve details about your organization and confirm your token works.
## Create an API token
Only Admins can create and manage API tokens.
1. Go to \*\*Settings > Integrations & dev > API\*\*. On the \*\*Tokens\*\* tab, click \*\*Create API Token\*\*.
2. Enter a \*\*Name\*\*.
3. Choose who the token acts as:
\* Leave \*\*Act as user or bot (optional)\*\* empty to give the token its own identity. Pick a \*\*Role\*\* to control what it can access, and optionally upload an icon.
\* Or select a teammate or bot. The token uses that user's current role and permissions.
4. Optionally, add an \*\*IP allowlist\*\* (see below).
5. Click \*\*Create\*\* and copy the token. Pylon shows it only once.
Tokens don't expire, and their access is controlled only by the role. There are no separate scopes.
### Roles
A token with its own identity uses the role you pick when you create it. You can change the role later with \*\*Edit\*\*. Older tokens that have no role act as Admin.
A token that acts as a user or bot has no role of its own. It always uses that user's current role, so changing the user's role changes what the token can do.
See [Roles and user management](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/platform/roles-and-user-management.md) for what each role allows.
### Who actions are attributed to
\* \*\*Token with its own identity:\*\* actions show up under the token's name and icon.
\* \*\*Token that acts as a user or bot:\*\* actions are attributed to that user or bot.
### Bots
Bots are identities for automation, so API activity is attributed to the bot instead of to a teammate. Bots can't sign in to Pylon.
To create one, go to \*\*Settings > Workspace > Users\*\*, open the \*\*Bots\*\* tab, and click \*\*New Bot\*\*. Give it a name, an avatar, and a role. Then select the bot under \*\*Act as user or bot\*\* when you create a token.
### IP allowlist
Add IP addresses (for example `203.0.113.10`) or CIDR blocks (for example `203.0.113.0/24`) to restrict where the token can be used. You can add up to 20 entries. If the list is empty, the token works from any IP.
Pylon checks the public IP address your requests come from, so add the public egress IPs or ranges of the servers that call the API. Private addresses such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `192.168.0.0/16` never match.
A request from an address that isn't on the list returns `401` with the `invalid\_api\_token` error code.
## Manage tokens
The \*\*Tokens\*\* tab shows each token's \*\*Acts as\*\*, \*\*Token preview\*\*, \*\*Role\*\*, \*\*Created by\*\*, \*\*Last used\*\*, and \*\*Created\*\* values. From the \*\*…\*\* menu on a token you can:
\* \*\*Edit:\*\* change the name, role, or IP allowlist.
\* \*\*Duplicate Token:\*\* create a new token with the same settings.
\* \*\*Rotate:\*\* generate a new token value. The current token stops working immediately.
\* \*\*Delete:\*\* permanently revoke the token. Calls using it stop working immediately.
\* \*\*View Activity:\*\* open the token's request logs.
## Review API request logs
Only Admins can view request logs. Go to \*\*Settings > Integrations & dev > API\*\* and open the \*\*Logs\*\* tab, or choose \*\*View Activity\*\* from a token's \*\*…\*\* menu to see only that token's requests.
Filter by token, or choose \*\*All tokens\*\*, and by a date range of up to 90 days. The range defaults to the last 7 days. Each request shows when it was made, the token, who it acted as, the method, endpoint, response status, source IP, user agent, and request ID. Requests made with a token that was since deleted still appear.
Requests rejected for authentication or rate limits aren't logged, and older requests may not show a token.
### When tokens are revoked automatically
When a user is deactivated, Pylon deletes:
\* every API token that user created, and
\* every API token that acts as that user.
Before you deactivate someone who created tokens your integrations rely on, create replacement tokens from another Admin's account.
An Admin who has created Admin-role tokens can't be moved to a different role until those tokens are deleted.
